newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece extradites German woman in disco bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Greece extradites German woman in disco bomb probe.

text.p: Greece extradited to Germany on Thursday a German woman wanted in connection with a 1986 West Berlin nightclub bomb which led to a U.S. air strike on Libya.
Two U.S. soldiers and a Turkish woman were killed in the attack in Berlin's Schoeneberg district. Scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel were wounded.
Washington blamed Libya for the blast and bombed the Arab state, killing at least 15 people and wounding more than 100.
The German woman, 31-year-old Andrea Hausler, was arrested last October in Halkidiki near Salonika at the request of German authorities who want to put her on trial.
"She left on a Lufthansa flight from (the northern Greek port city of) Salonika to Munich. She was accompanied by German security officials," a police official told Reuters.
"When she was told that she would be extradited she did not object. She could have appealed the extradition decision," the official said.
Hausler was on vacation with her two-year-old son and boyfriend when she was arrested. Two other people were arrested in Germany in October in connection with the attack.
